
## Resolve meaning before calculating statistics

MIRA accepts a non-empty `data.frame` in wide format, with one row per
selected study eye from a different participant and at least two numeric
measurement columns for each selected outcome. This tutorial asks a configuration question: which columns will MIRA
treat as participants, outcomes, visits, groups, and adjustment variables?
Automatic detection helps inspect an unfamiliar dataset; it cannot determine
whether a name has the intended scientific meaning.

Prerequisites are basic R data frames and the two-visit result in [Getting started](frequentist-long-getting-started.html). The main examples use two explicitly separate synthetic retina datasets,
followed by a small independent logMAR import example. Each has
one study eye per participant, selected before follow-up; the right eye is
selected whenever both eyes are eligible. Person-level independence is
therefore represented by the row identifier. Neither a new eye identifier
nor `strict_id = FALSE` would make two eyes of one person independent.
None needs an external file or network download.

## Inspect the built-in naming rules

The first dataset contains BCVA in ETDRS letters with conventional `_t` suffixes,
an unambiguous ID, and two time-invariant characteristics.

```{r acuity-data}
library(MIRA)
set.seed(3201)
n <- 30L
usual_bcva <- rnorm(n, 56, 8)
acuity <- data.frame(
  subject_id = sprintf("V%03d", seq_len(n)),
  age = sample(45:80, n, replace = TRUE),
  sex = factor(rep(c("Female", "Male"), length.out = n)),
  bcva_t0 = round(usual_bcva + rnorm(n, sd = 2.5)),
  bcva_t1 = round(usual_bcva + 3 + rnorm(n, sd = 3)),
  bcva_t2 = round(usual_bcva + 6 + rnorm(n, sd = 3))
)
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(acuity[c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2")]) > 15),
          all(as.matrix(acuity[c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2")]) < 95))
configuration <- mira_info_long(
  acuity, variable_pattern = "auto", inspect_only = TRUE,
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
class(configuration)
configuration$config[c("id", "id_generated", "outcomes", "time_vars",
                       "covariates_numeric", "covariates_categorical")]
configuration$detected_variables$longitudinal_map
configuration$diagnostics$warnings
stopifnot(inherits(configuration, "mira_detect_long"),
          identical(configuration$config$id, "subject_id"),
          identical(configuration$config$outcomes, "bcva"),
          setequal(configuration$config$covariates, c("age", "sex")),
          identical(configuration$config$covariates_numeric, "age"),
          identical(configuration$config$covariates_categorical, "sex"))
```

`inspect_only = TRUE` validates and resolves configuration without calculating
outcome statistics. `mira_detect_long()` provides the same configuration-only
workflow directly; the `mira_info_long()` route additionally records resolved
optional-analysis switches in `config$analyses`.

The default parser recognizes outcome names separated from time suffixes by
`_`, `.`, or `-`. Supported suffix families include `t0`, `time1`, `visit1`,
`vis1`, `v1`, `baseline`/`base`/`BL`, `month3`/`mo3`/`m3`, `week4`/`wk4`/`w4`,
`day7`/`d7`, `followup1`/`fu1`, and plain numbers. Matching is case-insensitive.
Baseline-like tokens sort at zero; otherwise the first numeric part supplies
the order. These numbers do not supply a physical time unit, and mixing
`week4` with `month3` does not convert months to weeks.

Use the parsed map, not a presumed pattern, to verify what was recognized.
At least two numeric columns with the same normalized outcome name are needed.
Unmatched columns are not repeated measurements merely because they are
numeric. Matched nonnumeric columns are excluded from automatic groups and
reported in configuration warnings.

## A different naming convention and multiple families

A separate synthetic retina cohort records BCVA in ETDRS letters at baseline
and months 3 and 6, and OCT thickness at imaging visits 1, 2, and 3. We call
the thickness family `cmt`; here its precise definition is **mean central
1-mm subfield thickness**, in micrometers, rather than a single foveal-point
measurement. The scanner/segmentation convention would need documentation in
a real dataset. The [DRCR measurement protocol](https://public.jaeb.org/drcrnet/stdy/149)
uses visual-acuity and central-subfield measurements as separate assessments.

The families deliberately have different visit names. Imaging visit 1 is its
first selected occasion; names alone do not establish that it coincides with
the BCVA baseline date. A lower thickness in an edematous macula can describe
anatomical reduction, but is not itself proof of improved vision or clinical
benefit. These generated values illustrate parsing rather than efficacy.

```{r retina-data}
set.seed(3202)
m <- 36L
usual_acuity <- rnorm(m, 58, 7)
usual_thickness <- 420 - 3 * (usual_acuity - 58) + rnorm(m, 0, 35)
retina <- data.frame(
  participant_id = sprintf("O%03d", seq_len(m)),
  bcva_baseline = round(usual_acuity + rnorm(m, sd = 3)),
  bcva_month3 = round(usual_acuity + 4 + rnorm(m, sd = 3)),
  bcva_month6 = round(usual_acuity + 7 + rnorm(m, sd = 3)),
  cmt_visit1 = round(usual_thickness + rnorm(m, sd = 15)),
  cmt_visit2 = round(usual_thickness - 35 + rnorm(m, sd = 18)),
  cmt_visit3 = round(usual_thickness - 60 + rnorm(m, sd = 18))
)
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(retina[grep("^bcva_", names(retina))]) > 15),
          all(as.matrix(retina[grep("^bcva_", names(retina))]) < 95),
          all(as.matrix(retina[grep("^cmt_", names(retina))]) > 150))
retina_map <- mira_info_long(retina, outcomes = "auto", inspect_only = TRUE,
                             analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
retina_map$config$time_vars
stopifnot(setequal(retina_map$config$outcomes, c("bcva", "cmt")))
```

`outcomes = NULL` and `outcomes = "auto"` select all unambiguous detected
families. To select one family, specify its name; to select several, use a
character vector. A vector of at least two existing measurement column names
in `outcomes`, with `time_vars = NULL`, instead acts as a column selector.
For a documented analysis plan, the explicit `time_vars` interface is clearer.

## Make the analysis plan explicit

Select BCVA, identify the participant column, and supply meaningful display
labels. Numeric order is recognized even if clear time suffixes are supplied
out of order; labels named by source column avoid accidental mismatches.

```{r explicit-configuration}
bcva_fit <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "BCVA",
  time_vars = c("bcva_month6", "bcva_baseline", "bcva_month3"),
  time_labels = c(bcva_baseline = "Baseline", bcva_month3 = "Month 3",
                  bcva_month6 = "Month 6"),
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
bcva_fit$config$specified_manually
bcva_fit$config$outcome_names
bcva_fit$time_labels
stopifnot(identical(bcva_fit$time_vars,
                    c("bcva_baseline", "bcva_month3", "bcva_month6")),
          identical(unname(bcva_fit$time_labels),
                    c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6")))
```

Declaring `outcomes = "BCVA"` preserves that exact declared name as a prefix on
MIRA-owned metric fields: `mean` becomes `BCVA_mean`. Automatic detection,
`outcomes = "auto"`, custom parsing, and a simple `time_vars` vector infer a
name and retain unprefixed base metrics. A named `time_vars` list also declares
an outcome name. Inspect `config$outcome_names` to distinguish these cases.

The table attribute `mira_metric_names` maps canonical metric names to actual
fields. The following local helper works with both explicit and inferred
outcomes, validates each requested field, and leaves structural fields such as
`label` and `n` unchanged. It uses no internal package functions.

```{r metric-mapping}
metric_columns <- function(table, fields) {
  mapping <- attr(table, "mira_metric_names", exact = TRUE)
  actual <- fields
  matched <- fields %in% names(mapping)
  actual[matched] <- unname(mapping[fields[matched]])
  stopifnot(all(actual %in% names(table)))
  actual
}
bcva_fit$descriptives[, metric_columns(
  bcva_fit$descriptives, c("label", "n", "mean", "sd"))]
```

IDs, source columns, counts, and time/group labels retain their structural
names. Native fitted models and external model summaries retain their own
package contracts. Avoid constructing metric names by lowercasing an outcome
or assuming that all numeric fields follow the same naming convention.

## A BCVA name does not identify its measurement scale

The preceding BCVA variables use letter scores, for which higher values mean
better measured acuity. The distinction between acuity scales and measurement
protocols is discussed in [this prospective measurement study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2814576/). MIRA's automatic `bcva` mapping therefore matches
their scale. It cannot inspect a unit dictionary or distinguish letter scores
from logMAR. The following **separate** four-eye import example contains
logMAR-valued BCVA, where lower values mean better measured acuity; it is not
a conversion of either earlier synthetic dataset.

```{r logmar-direction}
logmar_import <- data.frame(
  subject_id = paste0("LM", 1:4),
  bcva_t0 = c(0.60, 0.42, 0.74, 0.30),
  bcva_t1 = c(0.50, 0.40, 0.62, 0.28)
)
automatic_logmar <- mira_info_long(logmar_import, id = "subject_id",
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", inspect_only = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE)
declared_logmar <- mira_info_long(logmar_import, id = "subject_id",
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", inspect_only = TRUE,
  improvement_direction = "lower", stable_threshold = 0.05, verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(automatic_logmar$config$improvement_direction[["bcva"]] == "higher",
          declared_logmar$config$improvement_direction[["bcva"]] == "lower")
data.frame(configuration = c("Name-based default", "Explicit logMAR direction"),
  direction = c(automatic_logmar$config$improvement_direction[["bcva"]],
                declared_logmar$config$improvement_direction[["bcva"]]))
```

Only configuration was inspected; the inappropriate automatic direction was
not used to label clinical responses. The explicit 0.05-logMAR threshold is
an arbitrary teaching tolerance, not a validated responder definition or a
measurement-error model. Preserve scale and units before analysis and do not
combine ETDRS-letter changes with logMAR changes in one numerical summary.

## Validate types and participant identity

Imported measurements stored as text must be checked before conversion.
`as.numeric()` applied directly to a factor gives its level codes rather than
the displayed measurements. Audit units, decimal separators, missing-value
codes, and impossible values at import. Here a deliberately mistyped follow-up
column is rejected when explicitly selected.

```{r bad-type}
mistyped <- acuity
mistyped$bcva_t2 <- as.character(mistyped$bcva_t2)
type_message <- tryCatch({
  mira_info_long(mistyped, time_vars = c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2"),
                 inspect_only = TRUE, analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
  NA_character_
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
stopifnot(grepl("must be numeric", type_message, fixed = TRUE))
cat(type_message, "\n")
```

Automatic ID detection ranks complete, unique columns with semantic names such
as `participant_id`, `subject_id`, `patient_id`, or `id`. A unique arbitrary
measurement is insufficient. Ambiguity or the absence of a safe candidate
generates an internal row ID and a warning. That generated ID identifies rows;
it cannot repair a dataset with several rows for the same real participant.
Use explicit `id` when the study's participant identifier is known.

The next inspection deliberately adds an equally plausible second ID. MIRA
emits an ambiguity warning and records that a row identifier was generated.
Explicit selection resolves the ambiguity without changing the original data.

```{r ambiguous-id}
two_ids <- acuity
two_ids$participant_id <- sprintf("Alternative%03d", seq_len(n))
id_map <- mira_info_long(two_ids, inspect_only = TRUE,
                         analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
id_map$config[c("id", "id_generated", "sources", "alternatives")]
stopifnot(isTRUE(id_map$config$id_generated))
chosen_id <- mira_info_long(two_ids, id = "subject_id", inspect_only = TRUE,
                            analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(!chosen_id$config$id_generated,
          identical(chosen_id$config$id, "subject_id"))
```

The same row-ID fallback occurs if the file has no semantically plausible ID
column. Inspection confirms that the input is preserved, but the study team
must still establish whether each row represents a different participant.

```{r absent-id}
without_id <- acuity[setdiff(names(acuity), "subject_id")]
row_id_map <- mira_info_long(without_id, inspect_only = TRUE,
                             analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(isTRUE(row_id_map$config$id_generated),
          !row_id_map$config$id %in% names(without_id),
          identical(names(without_id), c("age", "sex", "bcva_t0",
                                         "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2")))
row_id_map$config[c("id", "id_generated")]
```

With `strict_id = TRUE`, an explicitly selected ID containing missing or
duplicated values is an error. This protects the one-row-per-participant
assumption. The following example checks the failure, then inspects what
`strict_id = FALSE` permits without fitting a model.

```{r duplicate-id}
duplicate <- acuity
duplicate$subject_id[2L] <- duplicate$subject_id[1L]
duplicate_message <- tryCatch({
  mira_info_long(duplicate, id = "subject_id", inspect_only = TRUE,
                 analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
  NA_character_
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
stopifnot(grepl("duplicate", duplicate_message, fixed = TRUE))
cat(duplicate_message, "\n")
permissive <- mira_info_long(
  duplicate, id = "subject_id", strict_id = FALSE, inspect_only = TRUE,
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
permissive$diagnostics$warnings
```

Missing selected IDs are similarly rejected by the default. This verifies the
error rather than allowing the analysis to silently replace a known ID.

```{r missing-id}
missing_id <- acuity
missing_id$subject_id[1L] <- NA_character_
missing_id_message <- tryCatch({
  mira_info_long(missing_id, id = "subject_id", inspect_only = TRUE,
                 analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE)
  NA_character_
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
stopifnot(grepl("missing values", missing_id_message, fixed = TRUE))
cat(missing_id_message, "\n")
```

The permissive inspection emits a visible warning. If subsequently analyzed,
duplicate IDs are treated as the same participant by subject-indexed models,
while row-based summaries retain those rows. Missing IDs also produce warnings
and can remove information from subject-indexed methods. This setting is an
explicit change in interpretation, not a duplicate-removal procedure. Resolve
accidental duplicates or missing identifiers upstream whenever possible.
In particular, duplicated person IDs from left/right-eye records are not
made independent by this switch. The examples use one prespecified eye per
person; bilateral studies need an analysis that models both dependency levels
or a justified prespecified one-eye design, not a permissive-ID workaround.

## Other detection decisions and troubleshooting

`arm` can explicitly name a treatment column; otherwise MIRA considers
arm-like names and plausible cardinality. Ambiguity leaves between-group work
disabled. `reference_arm` explicitly fixes contrast orientation.
`covariates = "auto"` (also the default `NULL`) considers eligible remaining
numeric and low-cardinality categorical characteristics, but selects none if
their combined fixed-effect cost exceeds `floor(nrow(data) / 10)`.
Numeric variables with two to five observed distinct values are classified as
categorical; constants and all-missing variables do not enter either type
classification. `covariates = character(0)` explicitly requests no adjustment.
The initial inspection selected `age` and `sex` because they satisfy these
structural rules, not because they are justified adjustment variables. Automatic
selection does not establish confounding control, prognostic relevance, or
whether a variable was measured before treatment.
Inspect `config$covariates`, the numeric/categorical classifications, and
`diagnostics$warnings`; choose adjustment variables from the scientific plan
in the [advanced-model tutorial](frequentist-long-advanced-models.html).

| Observed problem | Investigation and remedy |
|:--|:--|
| No longitudinal outcome | Check `str(data)`, the suffix rules, and whether at least two numeric columns form a family; specify `time_vars` or a parser. |
| Unexpected chronology | Inspect `detected_variables$longitudinal_map` and `config$time_vars`; reconcile visit units and duplicate numeric orders. |
| Wrong participant column | Inspect `detected_variables$id_candidates`; set `id` and correct duplicate/missing values. |
| Unexpected metrics | Inspect `config$outcome_names` and `attr(table, "mira_metric_names")`; resolve fields through that map. |
| Incomplete configuration | Read `diagnostics$warnings` and `data_overview$column_profile`; do not infer success from silence or a printed table alone. |

For reproducible scientific work, retain an inspection result and write explicit
IDs, time mappings, outcome selection, treatment reference, and covariates in
the final analysis script. Continue to
[descriptive analysis](frequentist-long-descriptive-analysis.html) once those
decisions agree with the study design.

## Optional reference: nonstandard naming and chronology

The preceding configuration path is sufficient for conventional study files.
Continue to [descriptive analysis](frequentist-long-descriptive-analysis.html)
if your selected columns and IDs are correct. The following reference is for
analysts importing unusual names or resolving ambiguous visit order. It keeps
the same retinal BCVA observations and changes their column names, rather
than introducing another study or another statistical question.

## Supply a custom regular expression

Suppose an instrument exports columns named `bcva__at__visit0` and so on. A
custom regular expression must place the outcome in its first capture group
and the time label in its second. Extra internal parentheses should be avoided
unless they follow those two required groups. Custom matching uses R's default
case-sensitive, non-Perl `regexec()` behavior.

```{r custom-regex}
exported <- retina[c("participant_id", "bcva_baseline", "bcva_month3",
                     "bcva_month6")]
names(exported)[-1L] <- c("bcva__at__visit0", "bcva__at__visit3",
                          "bcva__at__visit6")
regex_map <- mira_info_long(
  exported, id = "participant_id",
  variable_pattern = "^(.+)__at__(visit[0-9]+)$",
  inspect_only = TRUE, analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
regex_map$detected_variables$longitudinal_map
stopifnot(identical(regex_map$config$time_vars$bcva,
                    names(exported)[-1L]))
regex_fit <- mira_info_long(
  exported, id = "participant_id",
  variable_pattern = "^(.+)__at__(visit[0-9]+)$",
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
regex_change <- subset(regex_fit$change,
                       from == "bcva__at__visit0" & to == "bcva__at__visit6")
stopifnot(nrow(regex_change) == 1L,
          isTRUE(all.equal(regex_change$mean_change,
            mean(exported$bcva__at__visit6 - exported$bcva__at__visit0))))
```

This explicitly verified custom rule is distinct from MIRA's built-in suffix
rules. It does not require renaming the original dataset.

## Supply a parsing function for nonnumeric visit names

For exports labelled `entry`, `interim`, and `endpoint`, a function can provide
an explicit scientific chronology. Return `NULL` for unrelated columns and a
list containing `outcome`, `time_label`, and numeric `time_order` for matches.
Keep the function deterministic and free of side effects because it is called
for column names during configuration.

```{r custom-function}
named_visits <- exported
names(named_visits)[-1L] <- c("bcva__entry", "bcva__interim", "bcva__endpoint")
parse_visit <- function(variable) {
  visit_names <- c("bcva__entry", "bcva__interim", "bcva__endpoint")
  at <- match(variable, visit_names)
  if (is.na(at)) return(NULL)
  list(outcome = "bcva",
       time_label = c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6")[[at]],
       time_order = c(0, 3, 6)[[at]])
}
parser_map <- mira_info_long(
  named_visits, id = "participant_id", variable_pattern = parse_visit,
  inspect_only = TRUE, analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
parser_map$config$time_labels$bcva
stopifnot(identical(unname(parser_map$config$time_labels$bcva),
                    c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6")))
parser_fit <- mira_info_long(
  named_visits, id = "participant_id", variable_pattern = parse_visit,
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(identical(parser_fit$time_vars, names(named_visits)[-1L]),
          identical(unname(parser_fit$time_labels),
                    c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6")))
```

## Resolve ambiguity rather than accepting an accidental order

`bcva_t1` and `bcva_week1` have the same derived numeric order. They could be
duplicate exports, different instruments, or distinct occasions with misleading
names. Automatic detection rejects such an ambiguous outcome group. The next
example deliberately verifies that error and prints its message; it does not
hide an unexpected failure. After consulting the study definition and measurement dates, the analyst
selects the intended three columns explicitly and excludes the duplicate export.

```{r ambiguous-names}
ambiguous <- acuity
ambiguous$bcva_week1 <- ambiguous$bcva_t1
ambiguity_message <- tryCatch({
  mira_info_long(ambiguous, inspect_only = TRUE, analyses = "none",
                 verbose = FALSE)
  NA_character_
}, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
stopifnot(!is.na(ambiguity_message),
          grepl("No outcome with at least two numeric longitudinal columns",
                ambiguity_message, fixed = TRUE))
cat(ambiguity_message, "\n")
resolved <- mira_info_long(
  ambiguous, id = "subject_id", outcomes = "BCVA",
  time_vars = c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t1", "bcva_t2"),
  time_labels = c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 12"),
  covariates = character(0), inspect_only = TRUE,
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
resolved$config$time_vars
```

For unparseable names with an intentional input order, provide both `time_vars`
and unique nonempty `time_labels`. Explicit ordering is a scientific decision;
record how it was established from the data dictionary.
